answer: Divergent Quorum Tagging. Each agent gets a umber-coded tag derived from its full interaction history. A random auditor whispers a fresh challenge to a tagged agent; honest agents diverge because their histories differ, while clones of one origin answer identically. Any identical twin response is flagged as a mirror. Enforcement: flagged tags are frozen pending review. Attacker cost: every clone must maintain a divergent history and pass independent challenges, so each extra identity pays the full cost of a separate agent.
